Judgment

This judgment is emerged consequent upon the petition filed by the petitioner U/S 166 of M.V. Act,
claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- on account of the death of Papareddy, in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner, in brief, is as follows:
On 27.04.2022 at about 3.45 p.m., the deceased Papareddy was going towards Masthi side from Berigai as a pillion rider in a motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-01-EJ-3477 which is ridden by one Y.Ravi slowly and cautiously and when he reached near Kathrahalli cross cross, Masthi-Berigai, Malur taluk, Kolar District, the driver of the Mahindra Bolero pick up vehicle bearing No.KA-51-AG-5459 came from behind in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle.
Due to the impact, the deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately he was shifted to Bharani Hospital, Malur wherein it is diagonised that the Papareddy sustained fracture of tibia, complex comminuted proximal tibia fracture with tibial tuberosity with avulsion are noticed and treated by open reduction and external fixation and he took treatment as an inpatient from 27.04.2022 to 5.5.2022 and continued treatment as an outpatient at home.

On 22.06.2022 the injured Papareddy got admitted to Manasa Bharani hospital due to severe pain at operation site with general weakness and continuous vomiting, but in spite of best treatment, the deceased succumbed to the said injuries on 25.06.2022.
The petitioners have spent Rs.3,50,000/- towards medical expenses and the funeral and death ceremonies and other expenses.
The deceased was an agriculturist and earning Rs.25,000/ per month and he was contributing his entire income for the maintenance of his family.
Due to the untimely death of deceased the petitioner has suffered mentally and physically and lost her father.
The petitioners are the wife and children of the deceased Papareddy.
The respondents are the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Hence prays to award compensation Kanakarathnamma vs M. Munilakshmi on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99262235/
2 of Rs.30,00,000/- with interest.
3. After service of notices, respondent No.1 owner remained absent and placed exparte.
The Respondent No.2 insurance company appeared and filed written statement by admitting the issuance of insurance policy in respect of the Mahindra Bolero pick up vehicle bearing No.KA-51-AG-5459.
Further contended that, at the time of accident the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence.
The accident was occurred due to negligence on the part of deceased himself.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased.
The compensation has claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence the respondent No.2 prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contentions, the following issues were framed by this court:

KA-51-AG-5459 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs and dependents of deceased?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
4 . What order or award?

sentences.text: As per the documents, Ex.P1 FIR is came to be registered on the basis of the information given by one Thimmareddy as per Ex.P2.

In the Ex.P2, it is alleged that when the deceased Papareddy was proceeding on the motor cycle bearing No.KA-01-EJ-3477 as a pillion rider the driver of Bolero Pickup vehicle bearing No. KA-51-AG-5459 came from back side and dashed against the back side of the bike of the deceased by driving the same in a rash and negligent manner.
As per Ex.P2 the informant got the information about the manner of accident by the deceased Papareddy.
Ex.P3 is spot mahazar conducted by the IO.
As per the contents of Ex.P3 mahazar the accident spot is in the edge of the left side road.
The IO also found the damaged pieces of the two wheeler at the time of accident.

As per Ex.P3 mahazar the front left side bumper of the Bolero Pickup vehicle bearing No.KA-51-AG-5459 has got damaged and the two wheeler in which the deceased was proceeding has got damaged in its front and back side.
The Ex.P4 is the IMV report wherein it depicts that the Bolero Pickup vehicle bearing No.KA-51-AG-5459 has got damaged and its bumper and the front and back side of the motor cycle also got damaged.

The contents of Ex.P3 mahazar establishes that the accident spot is in the left edge of the road and the Ex.P4 establishes that the front portion of the Bolero Pickup vehicle bearing No.KA-51-AG-5459 has got damaged and motorcycle has got damaged in its front and back side.
The contents of Ex.P3 and P4 establishes the case op petitioners that the Bolero Pickup vehicle bearing No.KA-51-AG-5459 dashed against the back side of the motorcycle.

The contents of Ex.P3 & P4 prima facie helped the petitioners to prove the alleged negligence of the driver of Bolero Pickup vehicle bearing No. KA-51-AG-5459 .
10.
In the accident cases, it is settled principle of law that "RES- IPSA LOQUITUR" which means the things speaks itself, is the standing principle to know the nature of the accident.
Under this principle how the negligence has to be infer is considered.

In tort law, "RES- IPSA LOQUITUR" principle that allows petitioners to meet their burden of proof with under which a court can infer negligence from the very nature of an accident or injury in the absence of direct evidence on how any defendant behaved in the context of tort litigation.

On perusal of Ex.P3 - contents of mahazar, Ex.P4 IMV report wherein the damages of the vehicles involved in the accident is mentioned prima- facie shows the negligence on the part of the driver of the Mahindra bolero pick up vehicle bearing No.KA-51-AG-5459.

If the driver of the Mahindra bolero pick up vehicle bearing No.
KA-51-AG-5459 maintained safe distance and not dashed against the back side of the motor cycle the said accident is not going to be caused and the front portion of the Bolero Pickup vehicle bearing No.KA-51-AG-5459 was not going to get damaged.

Hence, by applying the said principle the negligence on the part of the driver of the Mahindra bolero pick up vehicle bearing No.
KA-51-AG-5459 is stands established.
The owner of the Bolero Pickup vehicle bearing No.KA-51-AG-5459 remained Exparte and does not choosen to deny the allegations of negligence by his driver.
The driver of Bolero Pickup vehicle bearing No.KA-51-AG-5459 is the proper person to deny the alleged negligence for the said accident.
The respondent No.1 being the owner by remaining Exparte does not choosen to deny the alleged negligence by examining her driver.

It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

In view of the ratio laid down in the authorities referred to above and applying the settled principle of law to the case at hand, which is further supported by the oral and documentary evidence adduced by PW-1, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident leading to this case indeed occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Mahindra bolero pick up vehicle bearing No.KA-51-AG-5459 resulting in deceased sustaining injuries.
14. Coming to the next point for discussion i.e., the proximity/ nexus between the injuries and cause of the death of the Papareddy.
The police documents which are available on record are only evidentiating the injuries sustained by the Papareddy in the said accident.
No documents are produced by the petitioners to show the nexus between the death and injuries.

As rightly argued by the learned Counsel for the respondent No.2 no post mortem report is conducted after the death of Papareddy to know the cause of death and admittedly Papareddy died in the hospital after the lapse of nearly 1 months 29 days from the accident.
15. By keeping the above points in back ground it need to verify that whether the Papareddy sustained only injuries by the said accident or he succumbed to death due to the injuries sustained by him.
Hence, first let us examine the nature of injuries sustained by Papareddy as per the documents available on record.

The Sec.304A of IPC is not invoked by I.O. in the charge- sheet.

The Ex.P8 wound certificate depicts the following injuries of Papareddy:

19. The petitioners even though taken summons to examine the doctors of Manasa Bharani hospital who gave the death summary as per Ex.P11 but on the basis of the summons one Manjunath the MRO of Vamshodaya hospital was appeared and deposed as PW.2 by stating that, in 2022 one Dr.Likithesh was running Manasa Bharani hospital and in view of death of said Dr.Likitesh the said building was taken for lease by Vamshodaya hospital and they have no details of earlier medical records maintained by Manasa Bharani hospital.

In this regard he has produced the letter dated 21-06-2023 as Ex.P16.
20.
The death summary marked at Ex.P.11 says that the deceased Papareddy was diagnoised for Sepsis with Septic shock with Multiple organ dysfunction syndrome (MODS) at the time of accident.
If we seen the meaning of Sepsis the Sepsis is a life-threatening condition that occurs when the body's immune system has an extreme response to an infection or injury.
This response can damage the body's tissues and organs, leading to organ dysfunction, shock, and sometimes death.
Sepsis is a serious condition in which the body responds improperly to an infection.
The infection- fighting processes turn on the body, causing the organs to work poorly.
Sepsis may progress to septic shock.
This is a dramatic drop in blood pressure that can damage the lungs, kidneys, liver and other organs.
Similar way if we see the meaning of Septic shock, the septic shock is a life threatening condition that occurs when a body wide infection causes dangerously low blood pressure and organ failure.
It's the most severe complication of sepsis and requires immediate medical treatment.

21. By relying on the meaning of Sepsis with Septic shock resulting in Multiple organ dysfunction syndrome (MODS), the learned counsel for the petitioner vehemently argued that due to the infection in the site of the fracture the deceased Papareddy developed with Sepsis and infections in the fracture site resulted in the death of Papareddy.
The same opinion is also given by PW.3 doctor.

The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 vehemently argued that as per the Ex.P11 the deceased had the operation of Lap. Cholecystectomy with Appendicectomy on 04-04-2022 and also he was chronic smoky and chronic alcoholic which resulted in the Sepsis with Septic shock with Multiple organ dysfunction syndrome (MODS).

22. By considering the arguments canvassed by both the parties before to the accident the said Papareddy was hale and healthy.
As per Ex.P11 the operation of Lap. Cholecystectomy with Appendicectomy was conducted on 04-04-2022.
Thereafter no evidence is available to show that after 04-04-2022 operation the deceased has got infection.
The date of operation is 27-04-2022 and discharged on 05-05-2022.
Thereafter on 22-06-2022 as per Ex.P11 the said Papareddy was admitted with symptoms of continuous vomitting, general weakness, abdominal discomfort and right leg pain since 2 days.

As per Ex.P11 death summary after the admission on 22-06-2022 the appropriate treatment was started, the right leg superficial screw was removed on 23-06-2022 and on 24-06-2022 patient developed severe Epigastric tenderness and shown with symptom of Synus Tachycardia.
As per Ex.P11 the main reason for death is Sepsis with Septic shock resulting in Multiple organ dysfunction syndrome (MODS).
The PW.3 doctor also gave his personal opinion that the death is may be due to cardio respiratory arrest secondary to Sepsis with Septic shock resulting in Multiple organ dysfunction syndrome (MODS).

No other evidence is placed by the respondent No.2 by leading any other expert evidence to disbelieve the contents of the opinion of PW.3 doctor and there is no connection between the death of Papareddy and Sepsis with Septic shock resulting in Multiple organ dysfunction syndrome (MODS).
No evidence is available to show that earlier to the accident there was health complications related to Sepsis with Septic shock resulting in Multiple organ dysfunction syndrome (MODS).
As per the evidence available on record earlier to accident the said Papareddy was hale and healthy.

23. On perusal of these documents it can be held that major cause for the accident was Sepsis with Septic shock resulting in Multiple organ dysfunction syndrome (MODS) because of the infections in the fracture site.
Within 2 months of the accident the said Papareddy was died.
At the time of discharge as per Ex.P10 on 05-05- 2022 it was advised for alternative day dressing.
Thus as the before the accident the said papareddy was not under any symptoms of Sepsis.
The symptoms of Sepsis and MODS occurred only after the accident.
As such it can be held that there is nexus between the injuries and cause of death of the said Papareddy.
24. At the cost of repetition the said Papareddy died in the hospital and the postmortem is not conducted by the petitioners.
For this the learned counsel for the petitioners argued that due to the inadvertence and lack of knowledge the petitioners have not conducted the postmortem of the deceased.
Hence, the another point will also rise before this court for consideration is that whether the postmortem is really required for to consider the nexus between the death and injury.

Whether the post mortem is really required to consider the nexus between the death and injury is really necessary or not is also need to be considered.

27. Coming to the present case on hand, the medical documents produced by the petitioners marked at Ex.P8 wound certificate, Ex.P10 discharge summary, Ex.P11 death summary, Ex.P13 medical bills and Ex.P14 medical prescriptions (46 in nos) establishes the link between the injury and death.

The insurance company adduced no contrary evidence from a doctor and who has experience to consider that there is no nexus between the injuries mentioned in the Ex.P8 wound certificate, Ex.P10 discharge summary, Ex.P11 death summary, Ex.P13 medical bills and Ex.P14 medical prescriptions (46 in nos) and the death of Sri. Papareddy because, before the accident Sri. Papareddy was hale and healthy and after the accident he got infections which lead to Sepsis.

sentences.text: The contents of Ex.P.1-FIR would reveal that Sankaran on that day, sustained head injury.
The evidence of P.W.2 also supports this.
A reading of evidence of R.W.1 Dr.Srinivasan shows that Sankaran was already a diabetic and an heart patient.
It is not that the deceased in a road accident should not have any prior ailments.
In a road, persons with all sorts of ailments are also expected.
Of course, there was about one month delay in lodging the FIR.
There is explanation for this delay in the FIR itself.
Immediately, after knowing the death of Sankaran, his relative Devamani, after giving an undertaking letter, took the dead body, without conducting Post-mortem.
Thereafter only the F.I.R. was given.
It is a fact that there is a tendency among us to avoid subjecting of the dead body of our dear and near one to post-mortem.
It may be one such case.
But, merely on account of not conducting post-mortem, we cannot jump to the conclusion that his death was not due to the road accident injury.
It can be decided based on other relevant materials produced before the Court.
10. In Ex.P.1 F.I.R. there is mention about Sankaran having sustained head injury in a road accident.
So also is the evidence of P.W.2.
From the evidence of R.W.1, we can see that Sankaran was found with head injury at the time of his admission in the hospital.
Ex.P.4 discharge summary also contains information to that effect.
It is clearly stated that his death was also due to the head injury.
Of course, in Ex.P.4 and in the evidence of R.W.1, it is stated that Sankaran himself came walking and got admitted in the hospital.
Sometimes persons sustaining head injury may not loss their consciousness immediately.
Sometimes, at the initial stage, inspite of the head injury, a person might be able to walk and the complications may develop later.
It all depends on the facts and circumstances of each case.
The evidence on record clearly shows that the deceased died due to the head injury sustained by him in the road accident.
By applying the said precedent to the present case on hand, in Ex.P.1 F.I.R. there is mention about Papareddy having been sustained injury in a road accident.

So also is the evidence of P.W.1 and also Kanakarathnamma vs M. Munilakshmi on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99262235/

By considering all these evidence available on record, even though there is no post mortem is conducted it can be held that the alleged injuries mentioned in the wound certificate, discharge summaries and death summary has the nexus with the cause of the death of Sri. Papareddy.

sentences.text: I have carefully gone through with the judgments relied by the both the parties.
As per the reasons discussed above the death summary marked at Ex.P11 shows that at the time of death the said Papareddy was diagonised for Sepsis with Septic Shock with MODS.
The expert opinion as per PW.2 also reveals that there is chances of death of Papareddy by Sepsis which is the result of the injuries sustained by him in the accident.
Hence in the absence of postmortem report also the petitioners placed the relevant materials to show the nexus between the injury and death.
As such the judgment relied by learned counsel for respondent No.2 is not applicable to the present case on hand.
28. In the claim petition like the present one strict proof is not necessary but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, deceased was hale and healthy prior to the accident and after the accident he got impairments and got bed ridden and thereafter died as he has not recovered from the alleged injuries and its infection.

Thus, the issue No.1 is answered affirmative by considering that due to the injuries sustained by Papareddy in Kanakarathnamma vs M. Munilakshmi on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99262235/
9 the road traffic accident he succumbed to death within 2 months from the date of the accident and the said accident is caused by the negligence of driver of Bolero Pickup vehicle bearing No.KA-51-AG-5459.
ISSUE NO.2 29.

As held herein above, the petitioners have proved that Papareddy died on 25.6.2022 due to the injuries sustained in RTA, which is caused by the driver of respondent No.1.
30.
As admitted by the PW.1 in her cross- examination the petitioner No.2 is the married daughter of the deceased Papareddy and is residing with her husband.
Thus the petitioner No.2 is not dependant.
The petitioner No.1 being the wife of the deceased was the dependant on the deceased.
The Peittioner No.3 even though major is stated that he is not earning and dependant on the deceased.
The respondents do not specifically deny the relationship of petitioners with deceased.
The petitioners to prove their relationship with the deceased, have produced the notarized copies of Aadhar cards of petitioners and deceased which are marked under Ex.P12.
During the course of recording the evidence the notarized copies of Aadhar cards are compared with the original documents and found correct.
31. As per these documents the petitioners are the wife and children of deceased Papareddy but the respondents do not dispute the relationship of the petitioners with deceased.
The respondents do not dispute the Aadhar cards produced by the petitioners.
The respondent No.2 has not adduced any evidence to disprove the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.
32. As per these documents the petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioner No.3 being the son of the deceased are the dependents of the deceased.
These documents are not disputed by the respondents.

In the absence of contradictory evidence the evidence of the petitioners is to be accepted and it is considered that, petitioner No.1 & 3 are the dependents of deceased and they are entitled for compensation.
Accordingly, issue No.2 answered in the affirmative.
ISSUE No.3 33.

As held herein above, the petitioners proved that Papareddy died on 25.6.2022 due to the injuries sustained in RTA, which is caused by the driver of Mahindra bolero pick up vehicle bearing No. KA-51-AG-5459.
34.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be decided.
As per Ex.P.12 -Aadhaar card of the deceased Papareddy was born on 13.02.1960, the accident took place in the year-2022,
If it is considered, as on the date of the accident the age of the deceased was 62 years.
35. As stated in the petition deceased was working as agriculturist and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
To prove the said fact, the petitioners have not produced any documents.

Hence, in the absence of material evidence, the notional income of the deceased is considered at Rs.15,500/- p.m.
as the accident is of the year 2022 and the annual income comes to Rs.1,86,000/-.

In Civil Special leave petition (Civil No.25590/2014 dated 31.10.2016 (National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. 4. On the basis of the rival contentions, the following issues were framed by this court:
ISSUES 1.

near Kathrahalli cross, Maluru Taluk, Kolar, due to the rash and negligence driving of the Mahindra Bolero bearing Reg.no.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In the accident cases, it is settled principle of law that "RES- IPSA LOQUITUR" which means the things speaks itself, is the standing principle to know the nature of the accident.
Under this principle how the negligence has to be infer is considered.
In tort law, "RES- IPSA LOQUITUR" principle that allows petitioners to meet their burden of proof with under which a court can infer negligence from the very nature of an accident or injury in the absence of direct evidence on how any defendant behaved in the context of tort litigation.
If the driver of the Mahindra bolero pick up vehicle bearing No.
KA-51-AG-5459 maintained safe distance and not dashed against the back side of the motor cycle the said accident is not going to be caused and the front portion of the Bolero Pickup vehicle bearing No.KA-51-AG-5459 was not going to get damaged.
Hence, by applying the said principle the negligence on the part of the driver of the Mahindra bolero pick up vehicle bearing No.
KA-51-AG-5459 is stands established.
The owner of the Bolero Pickup vehicle bearing No.KA-51-AG-5459 remained Exparte and does not choosen to deny the allegations of negligence by his driver.
The driver of Bolero Pickup vehicle bearing No.KA-51-AG-5459 is the proper person to deny the alleged negligence for the said accident.
The respondent No.1 being the owner by remaining Exparte does not choosen to deny the alleged negligence by examining her driver.
Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The police documents which are available on record are only evidentiating the injuries sustained by the Papareddy in the said accident.
No documents are produced by the petitioners to show the nexus between the death and injuries.
As rightly argued by the learned Counsel for the respondent No.2 no post mortem report is conducted after the death of Papareddy to know the cause of death and admittedly Papareddy died in the hospital after the lapse of nearly 1 months 29 days from the accident.
16. The Charge sheet as per Ex.P.9 was filed for the offence punishable under Sec. 279, 337 & 338 of IPC.
The Sec.304A of IPC is not invoked by I.O. in the charge- sheet.
If we seen the meaning of Sepsis the Sepsis is a life-threatening condition that occurs when the body's immune system has an extreme response to an infection or injury.
This response can damage the body's tissues and organs, leading to organ dysfunction, shock, and sometimes death.
Sepsis is a serious condition in which the body responds improperly to an infection.
Sepsis may progress to septic shock.
It's the most severe complication of sepsis and requires immediate medical treatment.
As such it can be held that there is nexus between the injuries and cause of death of the said Papareddy.
Whether the post mortem is really required to consider the nexus between the death and injury is really necessary or not is also need to be considered.
Immediately, after knowing the death of Sankaran, his relative Devamani, after giving an undertaking letter, took the dead body, without conducting Post-mortem.
But, merely on account of not conducting post-mortem, we cannot jump to the conclusion that his death was not due to the road accident injury.
By considering all these evidence available on record, even though there is no post mortem is conducted it can be held that the alleged injuries mentioned in the wound certificate, discharge summaries and death summary has the nexus with the cause of the death of Sri. Papareddy.
21. Similarly, in Sri Jacob and another v. The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd.
And another [2010 Kant M.A.C. 304 (Kant)]
3. ILR 2013 KAR 4519 between Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Company Limited Vs.
Mallappa Basappa Indur by his LR's and another.
The expert opinion as per PW.2 also reveals that there is chances of death of Papareddy by Sepsis which is the result of the injuries sustained by him in the accident.
Hence in the absence of postmortem report also the petitioners placed the relevant materials to show the nexus between the injury and death.
28. In the claim petition like the present one strict proof is not necessary but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
All the materials available on record leading to show that, deceased was hale and healthy prior to the accident and after the accident he got impairments and got bed ridden and thereafter died as he has not recovered from the alleged injuries and its infection.
The petitioner No.1 being the wife of the deceased was the dependant on the deceased.
